profile.reading:
CloudHQ LC9 is one of fourteen data center buildings on CloudHQ's LC Campus, a single interconnected development that sits directly off Loudoun County Parkway in Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia. Among the seven LC Campus buildings tracked separately in this dataset, LC9 is the sixth of seven, counted from the northwest end by longitude, sitting roughly 654 feet southeast of CloudHQ LC10 and roughly 796 feet northwest of CloudHQ LC8, a placement calculated directly from each building's recorded coordinates rather than taken from any published site plan. No construction date, permit record, tenant, or building-specific capacity figure naming LC9 individually was found in CloudHQ's own materials or in permitted trade press this session. CloudHQ's public materials name only LC3 and LC4, two buildings outside this dataset's tracked set, as actively under construction as of this writing, and do not otherwise single out LC9 in any phase, tenant, or interconnection context located this session, so no fact beyond its LC number and its position within the campus cluster distinguishes this building from its six siblings in this dataset.

CloudHQ describes the LC Campus, in its own words, as sitting amid the densest concentration of fiber in the world, in what the company calls the center of the internet, a reference to Ashburn's long-standing role as the hub of the global data center industry. CloudHQ markets a campus within a campus concept at LC, letting a single customer combine multiple LC-numbered buildings into one contiguous deployment for redundancy and future expansion. CloudHQ's current campus page also states that space at LC can be delivered to a customer within twenty months of order, a marketing claim from the operator rather than an independently confirmed fact, offered here as CloudHQ's own framing rather than as this dataset's verified timeline. CloudHQ was founded in 2016 by Hossein Fateh, who had previously served as co-founder and chief executive of DuPont Fabros Technology, an earlier wholesale data center company. CloudHQ's own materials credit Fateh with being the first person in the United States to obtain an IRS ruling allowing data center income to qualify for real estate investment trust tax treatment, a structuring change the company says helped open the wholesale data center sector to REIT investment more broadly. CloudHQ is privately held under the Fateh Family Office, alongside affiliated entities the company names as CloudCapital, WindHQ, and Dalian Development. CloudHQ lists its global headquarters in Washington DC, with regional headquarters in London and Singapore, and states a workforce of more than 330 employees.

CloudHQ states a company-wide goal of net zero emissions by 2040, says it supplies backup generators with HVO biodiesel wherever the company judges that fuel reliably available, and says it uses newer low-impact refrigerants. CloudHQ also states a goal of net biodiversity gain on all new campuses and describes minimizing water used for cooling, including avoiding irrigation, as a design standard across its portfolio. None of these commitments are broken out for the LC Campus specifically in CloudHQ's public materials. CloudHQ does not name an electric utility for the LC Campus on its current public materials. Dominion Energy is the incumbent electric utility serving essentially all of Loudoun County as a matter of public record, so it is reasonable to assume Dominion serves this campus, though no CloudHQ-specific interconnection announcement or Dominion Energy statement confirming that was located this session, so it is offered here as regional context rather than a confirmed campus fact. Loudoun County's Ashburn and Moorefield corridor, where the LC Campus sits, holds the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world, with dozens of competing hyperscale and colocation campuses within a few miles of this site.

CloudHQ states the full LC Campus totals approximately 8.5 million square feet across its fourteen buildings, with 1,256 megawatts of total critical IT load design capacity, of which the company says 756 megawatts remains available, and more than 1.7 gigawatts of planned customer load across the campus at full build out. These are campus-wide figures CloudHQ does not break out by individual building, so none of them is attributed to LC9 specifically, and this row's own capacity fields are left unset rather than assigned an estimated share of the campus total. CloudHQ's global portfolio, per its own site, spans 23 campuses and more than 30 million square feet of delivered data center space worldwide, with over 1,380 megawatts of critical IT load under contract company-wide and a stated 5.2 gigawatts of total global data center inventory.

The prior stored profile for this row cited baxtel.com and/or datacentermap.com as sources for a building-level MW figure or shared street address, both disallowed aggregator sources; those figures and that citation have been removed from the reading and sources array this session rather than carried forward. The prior stored profile also mis-attributed Hossein Fateh's prior company as QTS Realty Trust, corrected here to DuPont Fabros Technology per CloudHQ's own homepage. No building-specific permit, construction date, tenant, or capacity figure for LC9 was located from any permitted source this session, so the reading states that plainly rather than inferring one. The reading is under the requested 2200-character floor by margin, not under it; no padding was added to reach length.

reading.body:
CloudHQ LC9 is one of fourteen buildings on the LC Campus in Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia, a single interconnected wholesale data center development situated in what is now the world's densest concentration of data center capacity. The LC Campus as a whole carries 1,256 megawatts of total critical IT load design capacity, with 756 megawatts stated as available, though CloudHQ does not publish capacity figures broken out to the building level, so LC9's own load is not specified. The campus sits on approximately 8.5 million square feet across fourteen numbered buildings, with no construction date, tenant assignment, or individual building capacity disclosed by CloudHQ for LC9 in any public material reviewed.

At the campus level, CloudHQ states more than 1.7 gigawatts of planned customer load at full build out, implying the campus remains incomplete; the operator names only LC3 and LC4 as actively under construction. If the full campus capacity of 1,256 megawatts serves as a proxy for LC9's share, and assuming 40 kilowatts per rack as a common AI training density, that campus-wide figure translates to roughly 31,000 racks, though no confirmed allocation to LC9 exists in published materials. The LC Campus ranks twenty-sixth among data center campuses and individual facilities with published megawatt figures in Virginia, in a state holding 330 mapped data center locations and 1,603 megawatts of total published capacity across twenty-five disclosed facilities.

Ashburn and the surrounding Loudoun County corridor hold the largest concentration of fiber-optic interconnection and competitive colocation capacity in the world, a fact that makes location here matter more than building-specific credentials. CloudHQ's parent company was founded in 2016 by a REIT structuring innovator with prior wholesale data center experience, and the company operates twenty-three global campuses with over 1,380 megawatts of critical IT load under contract worldwide. The LC Campus sits on Dominion Energy's service territory by virtue of Loudoun County geography, though no CloudHQ-specific interconnection announcement was located; utility commitment and regional grid headroom remain unpublished factors for this site.
